frequency_question: How often do jurisdictions with a 0% active CCyB rate increase it to a positive level during a standard economic expansion phase?
membership_rule: Major central banks or regulatory authorities (e.g., US, UK, Eurozone, Canada, Australia) maintaining a 0% baseline CCyB under the Basel III framework, evaluated over rolling 42-month windows since framework adoption.

cases.name: Reserve Bank of New Zealand CCyB activation

provenance_note: 6 cases named, 16 claimed via skeleton x multiplier (2.7x)
coverage_note: 6 named representative windows across key jurisdictions; estimated population contains roughly 16 jurisdiction-cycle instances globally.
known_gaps: Varying domestic macroprudential frameworks mean different thresholds for activation, though all operate under the shared Basel III definition.
skeleton: Major jurisdictions (US, UK, Eurozone, Canada, Australia, New Zealand, Norway, Sweden) tracked across post-Basel III implementation windows, specifically examining instances where the buffer sat at 0% and was subsequently raised.
multiplier: 8 major jurisdictions observed across 2 distinct economic cycles (roughly 16 potential jurisdiction-cycle observation windows), with 5 total positive activations recorded from a 0% base.
validity_reason: Basel III capital framework rules and regulatory reaction functions remain stable across the medium term until a new global accord replaces them.
